title: Monthly sea-level persistence slopes gave no clear mean high-low difference at six US gauges in 1960-2025
abstract: We tested whether monthly sea-level anomalies have equal one-month persistence slopes above and below zero at six US gauges in 1960-2025. We removed calendar-month means and a quadratic time trend, then fitted a continuous two-slope model to valid adjacent months. The equal-site mean difference, above minus below, was 0.056. A circular three-year block interval from 4,999 refitted samples was -0.078 to 0.165. Adjusted site intervals excluded zero at none of the six sites. This is a descriptive test on selected gauges and a fixed NOAA snapshot. It does not measure flood duration or establish a physical cause. We include source hashes, monthly evidence, code, bootstrap weights, and an independent numerical audit.

display.caption: Monthly anomaly slopes and above-minus-below differences. Site intervals have a six-comparison adjustment.
